mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Electronic official certification accepted domestically; if used abroad, Hague Apostille through the Spanish Ministry of Justice

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized public deed of incorporation (Escritura Pública de Constitución)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Executed by notary in Spain; no apostille required for domestic registration; apostille only required for foreign use

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for shareholder representatives and signing officers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in country of origin or Consulate of Spain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing state is party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization through the Spanish Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary, issuing government authority, or Spanish Consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; sworn Spanish translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / corporate registry extract of any legal entity shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registry or trade registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; official Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration and enhanced due diligence dossier (PEP, OFAC, UN sanctions screening)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish law firm / external AML compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature in Spain; no apostille required if not leaving the domestic Spanish legal sphere

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced client due diligence under Ley 10/2010: all directors, shareholders, signatories, and UBOs must be screened against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, Spanish domestic terrorism and organised crime lists, OFAC SDN List, and PEP databases maintained by SEPBLAC, the Bank of Spain, and the CNMV. Continuous monitoring is required for the duration of the business relationship, with mandatory STR filings for any adverse hit.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) — Electronic name reservation via Sede Electrónica del Registro Mercantil Central (www.rmc.es) 'Denominaciones Sociales' service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Spanish or naturalized Spanish transliteration using Latin characters; names must not be identical or phonetically confusingly similar to existing Spanish companies; the legal form acronym 'S.L.' or 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' must be stated in the name; foreign words are only accepted where sufficiently integrated or accompanied by a sworn translation; names must not mislead as to company object, size, or territorial scope.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within one month of a negative name rejection, the applicant may file a recurso de alzada with the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado (DGRN) of the Ministry of Justice, attaching the original certification application and the registry's rejection notification. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately submit a new name application to the Registro Mercantil Central. If the administrative appeal is dismissed, the applicant may challenge the decision before the Civil Courts of Madrid.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable as the sole registered office for a dangerous goods forwarding company; a physical, accessible registered office in Spain is mandatory under corporate law and for SEPBLAC AML inspection purposes. A virtual address may be used only as a secondary correspondence address, never as the statutory seat or operational management location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High risk: unannounced on-site physical inspections are probable (>50% within the first 12 months) by SEPBLAC, provincial transport authorities, Guardia Civil logistics units, labor inspectors, and tax authorities, given the hazardous chemicals and high-risk AML classification of the ISIC 5229 activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), Articles 19-21, 22-41, 62, 209, 214
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) and Provincial Commercial Registry of the registered office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Incorporation (Escritura de Constitución)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SL requires minimum share capital of €3,000 (approx. USD 3,300), fully subscribed and paid in cash or non-cash contributions; a bank certificate confirming payment is required, no escrow account is required because the full amount must be paid at the time of subscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: FIRST, that all founders' share subscriptions as set out in the Shareholders' Register (Libro Registro de Socios) are accepted, and the attached share subscription list is approved, including the allocation of quotas. SECOND, the registered office is fixed at [Address], Madrid, Spain, within the jurisdiction of the Madrid Mercantile Registry. THIRD, the following individuals are appointed: [Name] as Administrator (Sole Director), [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Compliance Officer for dangerous-goods transport safety. FOURTH, the Chairman, Administrator, or Secretary is authorized to execute, submit, and pursue all statutory filings, including obtaining the provisional tax identification number (NIF provisional) and registrations with the Central Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) – online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application in the official form providing up to five proposed corporate names. The registry verifies that no identical or confusingly similar name is already registered. Once the negative certificate is issued, the name is reserved for two months. The certificate must be attached to the public deed.
required_dossiers: Application form for certificate of no name conflict
Notarized identification copies of all incorporating shareholders
Statement of the proposed registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected, reapply with alternative names within two business days; request a formal reconsideration if the rejection was based on an error in the existing registry database.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Temporary Bank Account and Deposit of Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate account with a Spanish bank, deposit the full €3,000 share capital, and obtain a deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso). The certificate must be presented to the notary and state the identity of each contributor and the exact amount paid.
required_dossiers: Proposed articles of association (borrador de estatutos)
The negative name certificate
Passport or NIE of all founders
Bank deposit certificate confirming the €3,000 capital payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank blocks the account due to insufficient AML documentation, cure by providing the complete KYC package and transactional purpose statement (DG freight forwarding hazardous goods). Reapply or transfer the deposit to another qualifying bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Public Deed of Incorporation before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (Notaría) in the jurisdiction where the registered office will be located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All incorporators must appear in person or by legal attorney before the notary. The notary reviews the bylaws, capital deposit certificate, and shareholder identification, then formally executes the deed. Signatures are notarized and a certified first copy is issued for registry and tax filings.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate
Bank capital deposit certificate
Full bylaws (estatutos sociales)
Passport or NIE of every shareholder and director
Tax residence certificate (NIF/EI) of each corporate shareholder, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary observes defects in the projected bylaws or shareholder authority, execute a supplementary rectification deed (acta complementaria or acta de subsanación) before the same notary without restarting the incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF Provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before registry inscription, submit Form 036/030 requesting the provisional NIF for the company. Provide the notarized deed, identification of principal administrators, and intended activities. AEAT will issue a provisional NIF valid until the definitive NIF is obtained after registration.
required_dossiers: Fully executed public deed of incorporation
Application form 036 or 030
Identity details of the administrator(s)
Statement of planned ISIC 5229 dangerous-goods forwarding activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT requires completeness review, rectify the form online within 10 working days; any failure to submit the NIF application before registration subjects the company to a late-filing penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the certified copy of the deed and the provisional NIF with the competent provincial registry. The registrar conducts a legality review (calificación) and, upon approval, records the company in the register. The company acquires legal personality on registration.
required_dossiers: First certified copy of the public deed of incorporation
Provisional NIF certificate from AEAT
Previous negative name certificate
Payment receipt of the registry fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a notice of defects (nota de calificación), cure by filing a rectified deed or making the requested clarifications within the two-month corrective period; otherwise the name reservation expires and the process must be re-filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Definitive NIF, Social Security Registration and Beneficial Ownership Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Tax Administration Agency (AEAT), General Treasury of Social Security (TGSS), and Central Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registry inscription, file Form 036 again to obtain the definitive NIF. Register the company and its directors in the TGSS social security regime. File the beneficial ownership report with the Central Commercial Registry in accordance with Real Decreto 304/2014, disclosing all direct and indirect owners.
required_dossiers: Registry certificate of incorporation
Provisional NIF certificate
Forms 036 (final NIF) and TA.6 for employer registration
Beneficial ownership statement
Director identification documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If TGSS or the Central Registry reject the filing, correct incomplete data within 20 clear days and resubmit; late registration can be cured by paying a reduced penalty where the company proves the omission was involuntary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Transport and Sustainable Mobility – Directorate General for Land Transport (Dirección General de Transporte Terrestre)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Operador de Transporte (forwarding operator license) and Certificado de Consejero de Seguridad para el Transporte de Mercancías Peligrosas (dangerous-goods safety advisor certificate)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge – Directorate General for Environmental Quality and Assessment (Dirección General de Calidad y Evaluación Ambiental)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Classified under Annex II.8 of Ley 21/2013 (storage) requiring a simplified environmental authorization, or a municipal activity license, unless the hazardous-goods storage quantity exceeds the thresholds of Annex I, in which case a full EIA Report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with RD 509/1996 and local sewer ordinances (e.g., COD < 500 mg/L, BOD5 < 250 mg/L). Fugitive VOC emissions from storage and handling must satisfy RD 1042/2017 containment levels. Dangerous goods must be stored with adequate segregation distances and secondary containment according to ADR/RID and national protocol.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (Certificado de protección contra incendios) from the regional fire service for any warehouse or transshipment facility; structural load inspection and low-voltage electrical installation legalization; occupational health and safety compliance under Law 31/1995 (Prevención de Riesgos Laborales), including a workplace risk assessment and emergency response plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — State Tax Administration Agency of Spain; official electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT at sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; customs administration for exports and special taxes is exercised by the Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales of AEAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: To obtain the statutory NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) for a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) dedicated to dangerous-goods forwarding: (1) acquire a Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social (negative name certificate) from the Registro Mercantil Central; (2) execute the public incorporation deed (Escritura de Constitución) before a Spanish notary; (3) inscribe the deed at the relevant Provincial Mercantile Registry; (4) file Form 036 (Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores) with AEAT to obtain the provisional corporate NIF; and (5) after definitive registry inscription, resubmit Form 036 to activate the conclusive NIF (format: letter plus 7 digits plus control character). The SL is simultaneously enrolled for Corporate Income Tax (Modelo 200 under Ley 27/2014), VAT (Modelo 390 annual return under Ley 37/1992), and, where staff are engaged, employer and withholding registrations; the ISIC 5229 activity and the special 'dangerous goods operator' licence declaration are recorded in the census (IAE classification). A non-resident foreign parent may lawfully hold 100% of the SL subject to no local counterpart requirement. A non-resident entity not having a permanent establishment must separately obtain an NIF/NIE via Form 030 (or Form 036 through a fiscal representative), file Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) on Modelo 216, and may be required to appoint a fiscal representative for IRNR and customs procedures.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SL is a per-se corporate taxpayer; Spain does not provide any US-style 'check-the-box' pass-through election. Available statutory elections include: (a) Group VAT registration (Régimen Especial del Grupo de Entidades) under arts. 126 et seq. LIVA, electable for Spanish-resident related entities meeting 50% voting control and board-appointment rights; (b) Corporate Income Tax consolidation (Régimen de Consolidación Fiscal) under arts. 56-100 LIS, requiring at least 70% direct or indirect ownership (75% where the parent is listed) of Spanish-resident entities and a formal application; (c) the participation exemption and ETVE holdings regimes under art. 21 LIS for foreign-sourced dividends and capital gains; (d) hybrid mismatch and reverse-hybrid transparent-entity rules transposing ATAD (Directive 2016/1164) and ATAD 2 (Directive 2017/952); (e) the reduced 15% CIT regime for newly-created entities on the first EUR 300,000 of taxable base (art. 29.3 LIS); and (f) customs facilitation statuses such as Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) and 'exportador autorizado' (approved exporter). Pass-through treatment cannot be elected post-incorporation for the SL; shareholder-level taxation is confined to dividend and participation exemption rather than flow-through of profits.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA — Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (Spanish Value Added Tax), harmonised with Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis annual turnover threshold exists for standard IVA registration: a Spanish-established SL must be registered with AEAT (Form 036/037) before performing its first taxable transaction. For qualifying small businesses, the simplified regime (Régimen Simplificado, módulos) applies to listed activities with prior-year turnover not exceeding EUR 250,000, and the retail surcharge regime (Recargo de Equivalencia) applies to retailers with prior-year turnover not exceeding EUR 1,000,000; a full-IVA DG freight forwarder claiming input VAT on hydrocarbon/chemical logistics will generally fall outside these restricted schemes. Intra-EU cross-border distance sales of goods into Spain oblige registration once the seller's total EU-wide distance-sales exceed EUR 10,000 (EU OSS threshold); non-EU suppliers maintaining Spanish warehousing or e-commerce fulfilment connectivity must register irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain mandates a layered electronic-invoicing framework: Ley 18/2022 'Crea y Crece' and Real Decreto 1007/2023 ('Verifactu') require all established businesses to issue, transmit, and archive interoperable structured e-invoices (Facturae XML, EDI, or PEPPOL standards) in B2B relationships, phased in from 2024/2025 with full sectoral application by 2026. Large enterprises (turnover exceeding EUR 6,010,121.04) inscribed in the AEAT Large Enterprise registry, VAT groups, and taxpayers applying certain monthly-refund regimes must additionally comply with the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información del IVA): invoice and book-record data must be transmitted electronically to AEAT in near-real-time, nominally within 4 calendar days following the end of the period in which the invoice is issued or received. Verifactu-certified cash-register/invoicing software must guarantee invoice integrity through hash-chaining, immutability, and qualified authentication against AEAT; there is no physical 'digital stamp', but each compliant invoice carries an AEAT-compatible traceability identifier. Failure to emit conforming e-invoices or SII records results in denied input VAT deductions and administrative fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Spanish DG freight forwarder may legitimately claim the 0% export VAT rate in the following cases: (i) under art. 21 LIVA for supplies of tangible goods physically exported from Spain/EU territory to third countries, provided the export is evidenced by a customs export declaration (DUA/MRN) and commercial proof; (ii) under arts. 22-23 LIVA for services directly connected with exported goods — including international carriage, loading, transhipment, warehousing incidental to export, and DG handling services — where the provider holds the export documentation evidencing the destination outside the EU; (iii) under art. 25 LIVA for intra-Community zero-rated supplies to a VAT-registered customer possessing a valid EORI/VAT ID, supported by Modelo 349 recapitulative statements; and (iv) for international transport and ancillary services where the B2B place-of-supply rules (arts. 69-70 LIVA) locate the supply outside Spanish territory. Zero-rating allows full recovery of input VAT only when the physical goods flow, the customs exit evidence, and the financial settlement flow are mutually consistent; domestic DG agency commissions, local storage in Spain, and domestic road legs remain taxable at 21%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DUA / Single Administrative Document (SAD) export customs declaration with a valid MRN from the Spanish customs office of export
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) naming the Spanish exporter/consoor as shipper and evidencing dispatch to a non-EU destination
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list declaring the UN 4-digit hazard class and DG placarding references
Dangerous Goods Declaration under the IMDG Code (sea) or IATA DGR Shipper's Declaration (air), plus ADR transport document for any road leg
Proof of physical exit from EU territory: customs-validated exit confirmation, carrier manifest, or port/airport arrival certificate
Transport contract (FIATA-FCR, CMR, sea waybill, or charterparty) evidencing the agreed freight route
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103 wire evidence, or Letter of Credit settlement record proving remittance of the export price
Where applicable, Authorized Economic Operator documents and statement of 'exportador autorizado' for preferential origin claims
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT's indirect-tax and customs audit units (Fiscalización de IVA e Impuestos Especiales) perform documentary triangulation comparing customs records, invoicing data (SII), and treasury inflows before accepting export zero-rating. Where export evidence is missing or inconsistent, the 0% rate is retroactively recharacterised as 21% output VAT, with late-payment interest (interés de demora) and surcharge escalators (1%-20% under art. 27 LGT), plus pecuniary penalties ranging from 50% to 150% of the concealed VAT amount (arts. 191/201 LGT/LIVA). For electronic-invoice and SII failures, fixed penalties of EUR 300 per omitted or incorrect invoice record apply, capped at EUR 20,000 annually, with an additional EUR 1,000-10,000 where structured e-invoicing is wholly absent. Fraudulent zero-rating claims exceeding EUR 120,000 constitute the criminal tax offence under arts. 305 and 305 bis of the Spanish Criminal Code, carrying imprisonment up to 6 years, a six-fold monetary penalty, and forfeiture of subsidies and public-contracting capacity. Erroneous customs declarations on DG consignments additionally expose the operator to smuggling sanctions under Ley 12/1995 and to administrative suspension of the hazardous-chemical transport licence under REACH/CLP and RD 840/2015; in such cases the zero-rating claim is denied and environmental enforcement penalties may accrue. Spanish VAT law does not enact a strict statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline, but AEAT fiscal practice ordinarily assesses export proceeds to be credited within 180 days of shipment; any longer settlement term requires documented commercial justification, otherwise the export exemption may be challenged and clawed back.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España, operating within the Eurosystem under the monetary authority of the European Central Bank. Foreign-exchange restrictions are principally governed by European Union law, Spanish foreign-investment and anti-money-laundering legislation, and Banco de España statistical-reporting rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro and has no general exchange controls. Current-account payments, including imports, exports, freight services, insurance, salaries, dividends, interest and other ordinary commercial remittances, are generally freely convertible and transferable within the applicable banking, sanctions, tax and anti-money-laundering framework. Capital-account movements are also generally liberalized, but foreign direct investment, certain investments involving non-EU or non-EFTA investors, regulated sectors, sanctioned jurisdictions and transactions subject to national-security screening may require prior authorization, notification or post-investment reporting. An SL may normally remit dividends, loan principal, interest and liquidation proceeds to non-residents after satisfaction of corporate-law, accounting, withholding-tax, transfer-pricing, solvency and beneficial-ownership requirements. Banks may require audited or management accounts, shareholder resolutions, tax-clearance evidence, dividend declarations, loan agreements, proof of source of funds and evidence that the payment is commercially justified. Dividend distributions require distributable profits and must not impair legally required reserves or the company's net-equity requirements. Payments may be delayed or rejected where the bank cannot verify the counterparty, beneficial owner, transaction purpose, dangerous-goods activity, sanctions exposure or underlying documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement for an exporter to surrender export proceeds to Banco de España and no general mandatory conversion ratio or universal conversion deadline. Export receipts may generally remain in euros or another permitted currency in an account with a Spanish, EU or other appropriately regulated institution, subject to bank controls, tax records, accounting treatment, sanctions screening and applicable statistical declarations. The company should retain contracts, invoices, transport documents, customs records, bills of lading or air waybills, proof of delivery and bank confirmations. Cross-border payments and balances may be reportable for Banco de España balance-of-payments or external-position statistics when requested or when applicable thresholds and reporting frameworks are met. Cash or bearer negotiable instruments physically entering or leaving the EU at or above EUR 10,000 require the applicable customs declaration; intra-EU movements may also be subject to Spanish cash-control declaration rules. No conversion deadline applies solely because an export invoice has been collected.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for low-complexity euro collections and payments; low to medium for a dangerous-goods freight-forwarding business requiring documentary trade finance, multi-currency settlement, credit facilities or high-value international wires. An offshore digital EMI may lawfully provide services in Spain only if authorized under its home EEA framework and validly passported, or otherwise operating through an appropriate Spanish authorization or agent structure. The provider must be an authorized electronic-money institution or payment institution, must safeguard client funds, and cannot provide bank deposits or ordinary bank credit unless separately licensed. Payment accounts do not provide deposit-guarantee protection equivalent to bank deposits. The EMI may impose enhanced due diligence, transaction limits, prohibited-country rules, source-of-funds reviews and restrictions on hazardous-material counterparties. Use of an EMI does not remove Spanish tax, accounting, sanctions, customs, AML, beneficial-ownership or foreign-payment reporting obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement that every director physically attend a bank branch to open an account. Remote onboarding may be permitted using qualified electronic identification, video identification, certified corporate documents, electronic signatures and beneficial-owner verification. Each bank may nevertheless require an in-person meeting, a Spanish-resident authorized signatory, a branch appointment, notarized or apostilled documents, certified translations, or a live compliance interview. Banks commonly require identification of directors, direct and indirect beneficial owners, authorized signatories, controllers, principal customers, suppliers, jurisdictions, expected monthly turnover, payment corridors and the regulatory basis for handling dangerous goods. Non-resident directors and shareholders should expect enhanced due diligence and possible delays.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business classified as high-risk because it forwards, brokers or arranges transport of regulated hazardous chemicals, explosives, toxic substances, radioactive materials or other dangerous goods.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Company description identifying the precise role as freight forwarder rather than owner, manufacturer or unlicensed carrier; applicable ADR, IMDG Code and IATA Dangerous Goods compliance evidence; transport, customs and safety-management procedures; licenses, permits and registrations of the company and contracted carriers; named dangerous-goods safety adviser where required; staff training records; insurance certificates; customer and route risk-assessment policy; sanctions-screening procedure; and sample redacted shipment files.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership, non-resident shareholders, nominee arrangements, trusts or an inability to verify the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Spanish commercial-register extract; articles of association; shareholder register; complete ownership chart to natural persons; passports and proof of address for all relevant owners and directors; beneficial-owner declaration; notarized powers of attorney; tax identification numbers; and independent corporate-register extracts for foreign entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned counterparties, dual-use chemicals, military end users or unusual trade routes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty master file; end-user and end-use certificates; export-control classification; customs declarations; licenses under EU dual-use and sanctions regimes where relevant; screening results against EU, UN, UK and US lists as contractually required; route and vessel or aircraft details; denied-party escalation records; and documented approval by the compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or irregular incoming capital, shareholder loans, pass-through funds or payments inconsistent with the declared forwarding activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed shareholder-loan or capital-contribution agreement; board and shareholder resolutions; bank statements; audited or management accounts; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; tax filings; financing term sheet; proof of beneficial ownership of the funding party; explanation of expected use; and reconciliation from receipt through operating expenditure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multiple unrelated third-party payers, cash-intensive activity, payment-on-behalf-of arrangements or rapid onward transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written customer-payment policy; agency and freight-forwarding contracts; invoices and shipment references; three-way reconciliation of payer, customer and consignee; segregation-of-funds procedures; transaction-monitoring rules; prohibition on anonymous cash; customer authorization for third-party settlement; and management approval for exceptions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient evidence supporting cross-border trade payments or a mismatch between invoice, customs, transport and bank data.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoice; purchase or service contract; packing list; safety data sheet; export or import declaration; bill of lading, CMR or air waybill; certificate of origin where relevant; freight calculation; proof of delivery; insurance documents; payment instruction; and a transaction-level reconciliation file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, criminal allegations, corruption exposure, politically exposed persons or sanctions-sensitive intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent adverse-media review; PEP and sanctions-screening record; compliance questionnaire; anti-bribery and corruption policy; intermediary due-diligence report; litigation and enforcement disclosure; beneficial-owner explanation; remediation evidence; and senior-management risk acceptance where permitted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-Spanish documents, expired corporate records, inconsistent translations or inability to authenticate foreign signatures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent apostilled or legalized certificates; sworn Spanish translations where requested; certified copies; electronic verification links; incumbency and good-standing certificates; specimen signatures; and a document-control schedule showing issue dates and renewal dates.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a regulated Spanish or EEA bank account in the SL's legal name. For share capital, transfer funds from the shareholder's verified account with a payment reference identifying the shareholder, the SL, the capital contribution and the corporate purpose; obtain the bank certificate required for incorporation or the notarial file, then record the contribution in the accounting and commercial-register documentation. For shareholder loans, use a signed loan agreement stating principal, currency, maturity, interest, repayment terms, arm's-length pricing, related-party status and use of proceeds. Maintain a complete source-of-funds and source-of-wealth file. Banks may request the corporate deed, NIF, registry extract, ownership chart, board resolutions, loan or subscription agreement, tax residency certificates and evidence of the remitter's account ownership. There is no general Spanish FX purpose-code regime equivalent to systems used in some controlled-currency jurisdictions; the bank should use accurate SEPA or SWIFT remittance information and any applicable ISO 20022 or correspondent-bank purpose field. Record the transaction as equity, shareholder loan, intercompany service payment or other legally accurate category, never as a generic unexplained transfer. Review foreign-investment notification or authorization requirements, including national-security screening, before or after investment where applicable. Reconcile all receipts to the general ledger and retain records for AML, tax, transfer-pricing, audit and Banco de España statistical-reporting purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For ordinary euro payments, use SEPA Credit Transfer through the Spanish bank, with complete payer, payee, IBAN, BIC where required, invoice number, shipment reference and compliance information. For non-SEPA or non-euro payments, use SWIFT customer credit transfer, commonly represented by MT103 in legacy messaging or the corresponding ISO 20022 message, with accurate ordering-customer, beneficiary, intermediary-bank, purpose and regulatory information. For documentary trade, use an irrevocable commercial letter of credit issued or advised through a regulated bank under UCP 600, with confirmation where country or bank risk warrants it; use documentary collections under URC 522 where appropriate. Specify Incoterms, transport document requirements, partial-shipment and transshipment terms, insurance, expiry, presentation period, sanctions clauses and dangerous-goods documentation. Banks will screen all parties, vessels, aircraft, routes, ports, goods descriptions and documents. Do not use vague descriptions such as 'chemicals' where a precise lawful goods description is available. For freight forwarding, retain the underlying customer invoice, carrier invoice, customs record, transport document, safety documentation and proof of service. Outbound dividends, interest and loan repayments require corporate approvals, tax analysis, withholding-tax processing, treaty documentation and arm's-length support. Cash payments should be avoided and must comply with Spanish cash-payment restrictions and declaration rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized bank or investment firm, supported by a documented underlying exposure, treasury policy, confirmation, maturity, settlement instructions and accounting designation.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or corridors where physical delivery is restricted or operationally impractical, subject to counterparty authorization, EMIR requirements, MiFID II classification and appropriateness or suitability procedures where applicable. NDFs do not bypass sanctions, payment restrictions or local-currency controls.

Cross-currency swaps and foreign-exchange swaps for documented funding, receivable or payable exposures, subject to counterparty credit limits, collateral terms, valuation, EMIR reporting, netting documentation and board-approved risk limits.

Currency options, collars and structured hedges may be used only after assessment of suitability, premium, leverage, downside exposure, accounting treatment and early-termination rights. Complex products should be restricted to appropriately classified professional clients and approved counterparties.

Hedges should be matched to forecast or contracted exposures, recorded under a written treasury policy, monitored for effectiveness, and executed only with regulated counterparties under appropriate master documentation such as ISDA and collateral support arrangements where relevant.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the annual accounts at the shareholders' meeting; approval must occur within six months of fiscal year-end (calendar-year entities: filing due by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers fines (€200–€2,000) and 'cierre registral' preventing further registry filings; failure to file for three consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 days following the six-month period after the tax year end; for calendar-year taxpayers, due by 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 5%–20% of the tax due plus 1% monthly interest; non-filing may trigger fines from €300 to €20,000 and an official assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Declaration (Declaración Anual de Titular Real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the annual accounts deposit; UBO changes must also be filed within 10 calendar days of each change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under Law 10/2010 for non-delivery or inaccuracy, up to €100,000 for serious infringement, plus possible civil/criminal liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Information Return on Third-Party Transactions (Modelo 347)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, filed in February of the following year (typically 1–28 February; if the 28th is a Saturday/Sunday, the deadline shifts to the next business day)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty from €150 to €6,000 for incorrect or omitted returns, plus late-payment interest and possible administrative sanctions

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required if, at the fiscal year-end, the SL exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive years: total assets > €2,850,000; net annual turnover > €5,700,000; average workforce > 50 employees
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General Contable - Real Decreto 1514/2007) for individual annual accounts; IFRS as endorsed by the EU for consolidated accounts where the group has listed parent undertakings

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must maintain an internal Beneficial Owner Register (Libro de Titularidades Reales) and confirm beneficial ownership information to the Commercial Registry during the annual accounts deposit. Any share transfer or UBO change must be filed with the Registry within 10 calendar days of the change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors / Minutes of Meetings (Libro de Actas del Consejo de Administración)
Inventory and Annual Accounts Book (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 300 – EUR 900 (approx. USD 330 – USD 990) for a professional registered office/virtual address in Madrid or Barcelona; lower in provincial cities
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 8,000 – EUR 25,000 (approx. USD 8,800 – USD 27,500) for a full audit of a DG freight forwarder with hazardous-cargo operations

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly organised SLs: 15% corporate income tax on the first €300,000 of taxable base per year for the first two tax periods (subject to activity commencement and legal conditions). Available credits include R&D and technological innovation credits (25%-42%), patent box 50% exemption on qualified net income, training deductions, and digital innovation credits. No sectoral tax holiday applies to dangerous-goods forwarding; the statutory 25% general rate remains the headline benchmark.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return) – submitted electronically through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) portal at www.agenciatributaria.es
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing and payment within 25 days after the six-month anniversary of the tax year end. For a calendar year ending 31 December, the deadline is 25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting result: net book profit or loss before corporate income tax.</entry_description>
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the worldwide results of the Spanish resident SL, including Spain-source and foreign-source freight revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary adjustments to reconcile book result with taxable base; includes non-deductible expenses, transfer pricing adjustments, and tax amortisation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not complete this line; transfer pricing adjustments for cross-border DG forwarding fees with related parties must be recorded here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year negative taxable bases (tax loss carryforward).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the annual offset cap (e.g., 60% of current positive taxable base for entities with net turnover under €20 million) and retain evidence of the loss computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax liability computed at the applicable rate: 25% general; 15% for qualifying newly created SLs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the standard Spanish rate; non-resident shareholders are not entitled to use the SL's corporate rate for their personal income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, bonuses and deductions, including double taxation relief and R&D credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits available to the Spanish entity; a non-resident shareholder cannot report these credits on the SL's tax return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final self-assessment result: amount payable or refundable after quarterly provisional payments, withholdings, and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a refund arises, the managing director must authorise the payment details within the statutory filing timeframe.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a fixed penalty of €200 for each return (€300 for non-approved filing formats). Where tax is due, an additional late-payment surcharge applies: 5% within three months, 10% after three to six months, 15% after six to twelve months, and 20% after twelve months, plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75% per annum). Omission or false data may lead to a tax audit with penalties of 50%-150% of the evaded amount.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 232 (Annual Return of Related-Party Transactions) – filed electronically through AEAT where reportable related-party transactions exceed €250,000 per related party or where a real-estate transaction with a related party exceeds €6,000,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same filing window as Modelo 200: within 25 days after the six-month anniversary of the tax year end; for a 31 December year-end, by 25 July.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: NIF, corporate name, and Spanish tax residence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SL files under its own NIF; non-resident shareholders are disclosed only if they are party to a reportable related-party transaction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the Modelo 200 tax period; a mismatch itself is a formal infringement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of each related party: name, jurisdiction, nature, and monetary amount of the transaction, including dangerous-goods handling fees, intercompany loans, or royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cross-border related-party transactions regardless of treaty relief; failure to disclose is independently penalised.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing methodology applied and benchmark comparables selected.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the arm's-length method; for logistics routine activities TNMM is commonly used, while profit split is accepted where both parties make significant entrepreneurial contributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of the documentation package prepared: Local File, Master File, and country-by-country report if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that any foreign-language TP documentation has a certified Spanish translation if required and is available for the invoice/payment period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-filing or late filing of Modelo 232 carries a penalty of €1,000 per related-party transaction or item of information with a minimum of €1,500. Inaccurate or incomplete disclosure carries €1,500 per item with a minimum of €3,000. If the omission conceals a transfer pricing adjustment, penalties under Article 114 LIS (15% of the adjusted amount) also apply.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% under Spanish Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) on dividends distributed by an SL to non-resident shareholders. EU/EEA corporate shareholders may qualify for a 0% rate under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the parent holds at least 5% of the subsidiary's capital and the shareholding has not been held less than one year.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must obtain an official certificate of tax residence (TRC) from the tax authority of the treaty country and provide it to the Spanish paying SL before the dividend payment. The TRC must be accompanied by a beneficial ownership declaration stating the recipient is the true owner of the dividends. The SL then applies the treaty rate (typically 0%-15% depending on the country and participation level). If the 19% rate was already withheld, the shareholder may claim a refund by filing Form 210 with the AEAT within four years, attaching the TRC, dividend documentation, and evidence of Spanish withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Spanish domestic statutory rates are 19% for cross-border interest and 24% for royalties. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive exempts interest and royalties paid to an EU-related company having a 25% direct shareholding for at least two years. Bilateral treaties commonly reduce interest to 0%-10% and royalties to 5%-10%; the specific rate depends on the residence country of the beneficiary and the activity giving rise to the income. The Spanish payor must verify the recipient's treaty residence and beneficial ownership before granting the reduced rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File become mandatory when the Spanish SL's net turnover (importe neto de la cifra de negocios) exceeds €10,000,000. Below that threshold, simplified documentation is required for related-party transactions exceeding €250,000 per counterparty and for related-party real-estate transactions exceeding €6,000,000. The Master File is also required at the local level when the consolidated group revenue equals or exceeds €10,000,000 under Spanish documentation rules.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime analogous to offshore financial centres, but economic substance is embedded throughout Spanish tax law: (i) an SL has legal residence where management and control are effectively located; (ii) treaty benefits are denied to entities without genuine business purpose under the OECD MLI/limitation-on-benefits concept; and (iii) ATAD and the General Tax Law anti-abuse clause recharacterise artificial arrangements. A dangerous-goods-forwarding SL that functions merely as a letterbox, with no local personnel, premises, commercial decision-making, or physical handling of regulated goods, may be reassessed, denied treaty relief, and subject to criminal tax fraud charges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting cash-based or letter-of-credit freight revenue, using fictitious cost invoices, falsifying transport bills, or misstating customs valuation to reduce Spanish CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of 50%-150% of the evaded tax plus late interest. If the amount evaded exceeds €120,000, criminal conviction under Article 305 of the Spanish Penal Code carries imprisonment of 1-6 years and a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt under Article 43.1(b) LGT when they caused or ratified the fraud. Criminal penalties may include personal fines, travel bans, civil restitution, seizure of personal assets, and disqualification from corporate management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SL with no real office, staff, operational decisions, or commercial activity, while shifting profit to non-resident related parties through excessive management fees, artificial royalties, or intercompany loans.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment with inclusion of the full economic income plus 25% CIT and penalties up to 150% of unpaid tax. The European anti-abuse rules and Spanish GAAR may deny treaty benefits and disallow the entire artificial structure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign agreements or tax returns for the letterbox entity are exposed to civil restitution, disqualification, travel bans, and criminal prosecution for tax fraud or money laundering where the sham structure is used to move illegal proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or file the Local File, Master File, or Modelo 232; applying a fabricated profit margin for dangerous-goods forwarding services; ignoring transactions with non-resident related parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A transfer pricing adjustment is made under the arm's-length principle, with a 15% penalty on the adjusted amount under Article 114 LIS. Independent documentation penalties under Article 213 LGT range from €1,000 to €15,000 per transaction or deficiency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Spanish courts have held directors personally liable when they knowingly approve transfer pricing reports lacking economic substance, do not retain contemporaneous documentation, or otherwise cause the company to fail in its TP obligations; liability includes the resulting tax and penalty amounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash payments over the statutory limit for high-risk chemical forwarding, handling shipments from sanctioned entities, failing to file suspicious activity reports (SARs), submitting false dangerous-goods declarations, or using ML structures to conceal beneficial ownership of the SL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines under Spanish Law 10/2010 reach up to €5,000,000 or two-to-four times the value of the illicit benefit. Additional customs, transport, and environmental safety penalties may revoke the special licence required for DG forwarding; criminal prosecution may ensue under Article 301 of the Penal Code for money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are criminally liable for AML failures in a DG logistics entity. Conviction may lead to imprisonment, travel bans, seizure of personal and corporate assets, disqualification from board positions, and personal civil liability to compensate third parties harmed by the unlawful shipments.
